title: fix(telegram): keep table before blockquote/list as sibling, not nested or dropped
body:
Fixes #168366

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram rich replies nest a preceding Markdown table inside a following quote or silently omit it before a following list.

## User Impact

Tables and their neighboring quotes, lists, headings, code blocks, and paragraphs retain their authored boundaries. Tables at the end of a quote or list also stay in their container. Rich delivery and the plain-text recovery path preserve every table value. No configuration, schema, protocol, or SDK surface changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A native table previously consumed no Markdown IR coordinates, allowing an unrelated following block to share its position. The parser now reserves one whitespace coordinate for each native table and preserves it through quote closure and final trimming. Telegram can use ordinary block ordering; its table-specific ownership heuristic is deleted. The quote boundary is calculated once for both style and structural metadata.

Original fix by @dhruv1220; maintainer cleanup moves boundary preservation to the shared Markdown parser, removes the renderer special case, and extends the regressions to sibling and trailing-container cases. The contributor's ancestry and human co-author credit are preserved.

## Evidence

Validated head: `170f80fd67a7833d832543d82a1328628e6c6a0b`, after merging main `1041e5562854746ed2ebeac6aaf4fa89e1357397`. Contributor code ran only on secretless Untrusted AWS leases using the clean-main bootstrap, `--fresh-pr`, `--no-hydrate`, no instance role, no Tailscale, and `CRABBOX_ENV_ALLOW=CI`. The explicitly requested `r7a.xlarge` instances provided approximately 31 GiB RAM.

- Regression: **10/10 pass**, `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks-table-segments.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, **4.26 s wall time** on lease `cbx_f79179dc6dd7`. The five requested adjacency cases, heading/code siblings, separate quotes, and trailing quote/list tables assert independent shapes and full content in both blocks and `plainText`.
- Production-only negative control: replacing only `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts` and `extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks.ts` with the pinned main versions yields **5 failing / 5 passing** cases in **3.54 s**, including both reported defects. Tests remain unchanged. The contributor's original prefix heuristic also failed a separate-quotes probe before the rewrite.
- Full module/importer suites: **236 files / 2,910 tests pass**, **1666.27 s wall time**, covering the complete default Markdown-core, Telegram, LINE, and direct core-importer collections. The explicitly selected Telegram E2E files add **3 files / 37 tests passing** in **458.78 s**, and the loopback HTTP live-named file adds **1 test passing** in **11.03 s**. Total coverage: **240 files / 2,948 tests**, with no skipped selected tests.
- Types, lint, and format: **pass** for `pnpm tsgo:core` (70.43 s), `pnpm tsgo:core:test packages` (105.03 s, including extension declarations), `pnpm tsgo:extensions` (80.45 s), and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` (122.42 s). Remote oxfmt passes. [Canonical CI changed lint passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38083082680/job/114304347758), with the core lint shards also green. The manual all-files command using `oxlint.core.json` incorrectly places Telegram outside its project and reports an unresolved existing `MarkdownTableCell`; the repository routes plugin lint through `extensions/tsconfig.json`, and that correctly routed job passes. No source suppression or type workaround was added.
- Independent Codex review: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings**. This was a static review; execution proof is reported separately.
- [CI regression evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38083082680/job/114304078207): 10 cases pass, **0.084 CI seconds** summed from rounded case timings. The containing 7-file/189-test shard took 17.56 s (19.09 s harness wall); CI does not expose standalone file-process wall time.

### Real Gateway delivery proof

Fresh lease `cbx_fb9af8f1df7f` replayed the reporter's exact Markdown (including the bold quote and both list items) through a real isolated Gateway, the Telegram plugin, a loopback fake Telegram Bot API, and the QA mock OpenAI provider. Four main-production turns and four fixed-production turns passed: each reported input was delivered successfully as rich content and again through actual plain fallback after an injected `RICH_MESSAGE_ENTITY_INVALID` response. Main used the two production files reverted to the pinned base; fixed used the clean pushed head. Ports and state were isolated, and all subprocess groups were stopped.

| Input | Main outgoing blocks | Fixed outgoing blocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table then quote | `blockquote[table, paragraph]` | `table, blockquote[paragraph]` |
| Table then list | `list` (table absent) | `table, list` |

For the list case, main's actual fallback was only `• follow up Acme\n• send draft`. The fix sends `Brand | Status\nAcme | waiting\n• follow up Acme\n• send draft`. Headers, cell values, quote text, and both list items retain their authored counts in both corrected rich payloads and plain fallbacks; `Acme` occurs twice in the reported list input and twice after the fix. The four-turn runs took **89.97 s main / 87.49 s fixed**, including startup. Another eight Gateway turns with unique content sentinels also passed on lease `cbx_509169b55011`. This proves Gateway and Telegram-plugin delivery against the fake API, not Telegram Test Server or client rendering.

The first live harness attempt reached a successful send but waited for an outdated success-log message. The harness receipt matcher was corrected against the current send owner, then both modes passed on the fresh lease above. That attempt is not counted as passing live proof.

### Review and inherited CI failures

The latest full ClawSweeper review of this head found no code findings and rated the repair complete. Its missing behavior evidence and QA profile 2 attribution are supplied here. The campaign requires a secretless real Gateway with a fake Bot API; this evidence therefore does not claim Telegram Test Server or client rendering. Nested trailing tables are covered by the independent renderer regressions and full module tests. The original `check-lint` job `114191625449` failed only because oxfmt rejected the two original changed files; formatting is corrected and current canonical lint passes. There were no human review findings or inline comments.

The current CI aggregate remains red for **inherited QA failures**, not claimed green. `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` fails its private-completion projection assertion; `memory-dreaming-sweep` times out after 180000 ms with no promotion bus events. Both also fail in [scheduled main QA](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38084147216/job/114307136317), at main `b66d8da2938da040a1db9a83851d80d59320ff5c`.

PR CI used merge `921c32d976882873d3e745e7568427ef47480b31` (main `6b5284f579371f0e372b6c1882f863df19ffdb57` plus this head). It differs from that main parent only in this PR's four paths. The memory-core and memory-host-sdk trees and both scenario blobs match the independently failing main run. Both runs complete dreaming with `candidates=0, applied=0`; the cause of missing candidates remains outside this renderer repair. The memory scenario does not send channel messages and uses the memory owner's separate line chunker, not this Markdown IR.
